nal human input, JSONL storage and CSV export.
# dsh-coding-time

Local coding-activity timing for the DeepSeek Harness (DSH). It measures
wall-clock active time per

project (`cwd`), counts added/deleted lines from real
diff metadata, and can optionally time human e

dits. All data stays on this
machine under `~/.dsh` — no account, no network service, no telemetry.
Dark theme

The session header shows today's AI active time at a glance and opens a compact
summary popover.
## What it does

- **Active time by project.** Records wall-clock intervals of AI activity
(tool calls and assistant

events), grouped by working directory. Overlapping
intervals are merged into a union, so the total i

s never a simple sum.
- **Real line accounting.** Added and deleted lines come only from explicit di

ff
metadata returned by tools. Missing metadata stays unknown — it is never
filled in as zero.
- **O

ptional human timing.** Off by default. It becomes available only when an
editor integration supplie

s explicit real-input evidence.
- **Time by file.** Active intervals are apportioned across the file

s they touch
and shown as a donut chart, with a per-file share breakdown.
- **Project ranking.** Pro

jects are listed by union active time with a duration
bar and a percentage of the leading project.
-

**Daily activity.** A bar chart of AI (and, when connected, human) time per day.
- **Recent activit

y and file changes.** A short timeline of recent events, plus
a read-only snapshot of the current Gi

t working tree per project.
- **Settings.** Heartbeat, idle and flush intervals, collection switches

, the
local storage directory and storage statistics — all editable in the Host's
settings page when

a writable config namespace is available.
- **CSV export.** Download the summary as CSV; unknown va

lues stay distinct
from zero.
## How it stays local

The Web dashboard mounts onto the Harness's existing `webServer` — the plugin
adds no HTTP listener

of its own. It reads from same-origin local routes and
writes JSONL under `<storageDirectory>/<profi

le>/`. There is no third-party
API call, no outbound statistics, and no credentials stored or read b

y the UI.
Runtime code uses only Node built-ins; the settings form uses the Host-provided
`@deepseek
-ai/schemastery` peer dependency to build its config schema.

Uncollected or not-connected values are shown as such (for example "not
collected" or "not connected
"), never as a fabricated `0`.

y when the Host exposes this plugin's own writable
Config namespace; otherwise the client shows an e

xplicit read-only state and
